timed_text.text: Day 29, one last reframe, and this one goes the broadest.
The first two reframe exercises were about specific moments.
Today I want you to think bigger.
A period in your athletic career, a season, a stretch of months, maybe longer, where
it felt like everything was working against you, injuries, a coaching change, losing your
position, a performance slump you couldn't climb out of.
First athletes carry that period as evidence against themselves.
That's when I found out I wasn't as good as I thought.
That's when things started going wrong.
And here's what I've seen working with athletes who've been through that.
The ones who'd come out on the other side and competed at a higher level, they didn't
avoid the adversity.
They extracted from it.
The hard period didn't break them.
It built the part of them that's unbreakable.
You cannot achieve greatness without going through the difficult parts.
The suffering isn't a detour.
It's the training.
Think about your hardest stretch.
Not to relive it to extract what it actually built.
On your screen, go ahead and walk through it more time.

cards.prompt: Describe the hardest stretch of your athletic career. What was happening? What made it difficult?
What did that period demand of you mentally that nothing else had before?
What did you prove about yourself by getting through it — even if it didn't feel that way at the time?
Write one sentence: what that period built in you that you now compete with.

timed_text.text: That adversity it was an evidence against you. It was the training and it's in your evidence log now
Not history
